author: Paweł Krzywdziński
name: StateUI MAUI App
description: An application whose user interface is written in Swift: one page, a counter, a MAUI head for every MAUI platform and, with --appkit, a native macOS head beside it.
//sourceName: Every occurrence of StateUIStarter becomes the name given to -n, in file
names as well as in the files themselves. The token is deliberately not
properties, and they are the build's own, not this application's.

//applicationId: The bundle identifier is lower case on every platform, so the name has to
arrive here in that form as well - com.example.stateuistarter becomes

StateUIPath.description: An absolute path to a StateUI checkout to build against instead of the published packages - both halves, Swift and C#. Required for --appkit.

AppKit.description: Adds a native macOS head, Platforms/AppKit, beside the MAUI one. The AppKit host comes from a StateUI checkout, so this needs --stateui-path.

modifiers.//: Build products, in case the template was ever built in place.
The AppKit head, only when asked for.

//: THE BUILD SCRIPTS ARE COPIED BYTE FOR BYTE. The templating engine
EVALUATES MSBuild Condition attributes in the files it writes: measured
on StateUI.targets, it took the <Error> guards that say a Swift build
produced no native library with it. Nothing under .scripts/ carries the
application's name, so there is nothing to replace there.
